product_overview: Siyaq is a smart Islamic schedule management app that helps users organize daily tasks, routines, and sleep around dynamic prayer times. It provides dashboard, calendar, assistant, and settings views for managing time, prayer adjustments, and recurring schedules.
core_goals: Switch between the main app sections and customize the app appearance
View a daily schedule that includes prayer blocks, free time, and user tasks
Add and manage tasks with time ranges and conflict resolution
Adjust prayer offsets and durations to better fit personal routines
Create recurring weekly routines and special schedule templates

features.name: Navigation & Theme Toggle
features.description: Allows users to move between the main app sections and change the app theme mode.
user_flows: Navigate to / -> Switch between the main tabs -> See the dashboard, calendar, assistant, and settings sections update
Navigate to / -> Open the theme controls -> Switch between light mode, dark mode, and system theme -> See the app appearance change
Navigate to / -> Open the profile avatar controls -> Choose a different avatar -> See the selected avatar persist

features.name: Daily Dashboard Timeline
features.description: Shows a dynamic daily timeline with prayer blocks, task items, and free time slots that users can explore and edit.
user_flows: Navigate to /dashboard -> Scroll through the timeline -> See prayer blocks, task items, and free time slots for the day
Navigate to /dashboard -> Tap a free time slot -> See the task creation sheet open with the selected time range pre-filled
Navigate to /dashboard -> Select an existing task in the timeline -> Delete the task -> See the timeline update without that task

features.name: Task Addition & Conflict Resolution
features.description: Lets users create tasks with titles, descriptions, time ranges, task types, sleep mode, and prayer reaction preferences, then handle overlaps when they occur.
user_flows: Navigate to /calendar -> Open the task creation flow -> Enter a task title -> Optionally enter a description -> Select start and end times -> Choose a task type -> Choose a prayer reaction mode -> Submit the task -> See the new task appear in the schedule

Navigate to /calendar -> Open the task creation flow -> Enter a task that overlaps an existing task -> Submit the task -> See a conflict dialog appear -> Choose to trim or cut the overlap, or replace or delete the conflicting task -> See the schedule update
Navigate to /calendar -> Open the task creation flow -> Enter task details -> Enable sleep mode for the task -> Submit the task -> See the task saved with sleep mode behavior applied

features.name: Prayer Customization & Settings
features.description: Provides controls for adjusting prayer offsets, prayer durations, API credentials, and restoring default settings.
user_flows: Navigate to /settings -> Adjust the prayer offset sliders for one or more prayers -> See the prayer start times change according to the selected offsets
Navigate to /settings -> Adjust the prayer duration sliders for one or more prayers -> See the prayer block lengths update according to the selected durations
Navigate to /settings -> Enter a Gemini API key or an OpenAI API key -> Save the credentials -> See the keys remain stored in settings
Navigate to /settings -> Choose reset settings -> Confirm the reset action -> See prayer settings, theme mode, and stored credentials return to defaults

features.name: Weekly & Special Day Schedule Managers
features.description: Lets users create recurring weekly routines and copy routine patterns into special schedules such as special dates or Ramadan templates.
user_flows: Navigate to /settings -> Open the weekly schedule manager -> Add a recurring task for a weekday -> Save the routine -> See it available as part of the weekly schedule
Navigate to /settings -> Open the weekly schedule manager -> Select an existing recurring task -> Delete the task -> See the weekly routine list update
Navigate to /settings -> Open the template manager -> Copy weekday routines into special dates or Ramadan mode -> See the template schedule populated with the selected routine pattern
